chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Abi Salama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Death came to a man, so it was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has been presented with death.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood up, and with him were some of his companions, until they came to him while he was unconscious. He said, 'O Angel of Death, restrain from the man until I question him.' So the man regained consciousness.

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What did you see?' He said, 'I saw a lot of whiteness and a lot of darkness.' He said, 'So which of the two was nearer to you?' He said, 'The darkness.'
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Say, O Allah, forgive me the abundance of my disobedience to You, and accept from me the little of my obedience to You.' So he said it.
Then unconsciousness came upon him, so he said, 'O Angel of Death, lighten from him until I question him.' So the man awoke.
He said, 'What did you see?' He said, 'I saw a lot of whiteness and a lot of darkness.' He said, 'So which of the two was nearer to you?' He said, 'The whiteness.'
So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'May Allah forgive your companion.'
He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'When you are present with a dying person, say to him this speech, for him to say it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended words to say to a dying person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia practice of *talqeen* (indoctrination) at the deathbed, where the dying are guided to affirm the truth of the Hereafter by visualizing the light of faith or the darkness of disbelief. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies this narrative into a practical ritual, instructing companions to recite specific supplications to ease the soul's transition, emphasizing the intercessory role of the Prophet and Imams in the *Barzakh*. This reflects the theological belief that conscious affirmation of faith at the moment of death can influence the soul's immediate post-mortem experience.
